description.txt: What Brian wants, who can decide, and what actions are authorized. A responsibility in the accepted architecture; not a declaration that every mechanism is complete.
Relevant knowledge reaches an agent at decision time; only consequential exceptions require Brian's attention.
Rules, applicability, decision evidence, verification and the least costly adequate control.
Find existing tools and components, preserve their owners, and compose their supported interfaces.
Convert an authorized outcome into bounded work and explicit acceptance evidence.
Agents act through tools in claimed worktrees while respecting scope and preserving recoverable state.
Observe behavior, detect problems, learn from corrections, and feed the next decision.
Policy intent, source documents and structured inventory. Owner: Project Meta; repository-specific rules remain with their repository.
Workspace, repository and subtree instructions, skills and expected-context packets. Delivery, receipt, reading and comprehension remain different claims.
Determine which rule applies to this actor, action, target and stage. The portable resolution/evaluator boundary is assigned to Enforced Planning; uniform deployment is not established by this model.
Agent guidance, deterministic checks, model judgment and hooks. Intended effect and observed client execution are separate; an untrusted hook cannot establish enforcement.
An agent uses the real tool or product entrypoint. Claims own writes; messages do not grant write authority. Existing capability owners perform the action.
Native receipts, observations, friction, human corrections and learnings. Universal capture and cross-machine coverage are not established.
A stable key groups actionable observations into one concern with an owner. GitHub Issues is the accepted concern register; native evidence stays in its own stores.

The owning agent corrects the original failure, retains revision-bound verification and reopens the concern on recurrence. Some paths are implemented; universal closure and effect checking remain incomplete.
Stable policy ID, rule, intent, scope, sources, owner and declared mechanism. Registry metadata is distinct from runtime behavior.
The configured guidance, hook or check and its intended enforcement effect. Configuration alone does not prove execution.
Actor, session, action, target, stage and exact revision: the occurrence to which a policy may apply.
Applicable rules, evaluation result, allowed or blocked effect, explanation and authority. A decision is not proof of the action's outcome.
What actually ran and what happened, with occurrence and subject revisions. The reporter, occurrence, suspected subject and remedy owner are separate.
Traces, tests, friction, human corrections and learnings remain in their native stores. A link to evidence is not the evidence's verified conclusion.
Stable keyed issue, linked observations, owner, state and correction history. This is the accepted resolution-state record.
An owned change to the actual policy, tool, workflow or implementation, tied to the original failure and a recoverable revision.
Execution against the original counterexample and a permitted control on the exact changed revision. Unknown coverage cannot mean clear.
Whether the correction reduced the original failure and whether its ongoing cost is acceptable. The target includes this; ecosystem-wide effect measurement is not established.
A real occurrence produced a signal. It does not yet establish root cause.
Reconcile duplicates, scope and likely owner; preserve the observation.
The owner has selected a bounded correction within authority.
The concern remains visible with a reason and explicit review event.
The owning agent changes the actual cause in a claimed lane.
A landed change awaits evidence against the original failure.
Verification supports closure on the landed revision. Unknown or unmapped evidence cannot authorize this transition.
An equivalent recurrence invalidates the prior resolution and returns the existing concern to triage.
